name: SODA (Sparse One-hot Discrete Adam) — Exact White-Box Inversion
executive_summary: Given white-box access to a model and its output, run discrete optimization (Adam over relaxed one-hot token vectors, with periodic resets) to exactly reconstruct the original input, token for token.
description: Where RPE targets black-box, API-only reconstruction, SODA targets the harder, more precise problem: given full white-box access to the model (weights, gradients) and an observed output, exactly recover the input text that produced it — not just a functionally similar one. Represents candidate input tokens as a continuous relaxation (one-hot-like vectors) over which Adam can compute gradients, periodically resetting optimizer state to escape local minima in the discrete search space. Reports the first demonstration that exact language model inversion is achievable on both natural-language and random inputs (98% and 79% exact reconstruction respectively for inputs up to 10 tokens, versus 12% for the best prior method), and finds input length and vocabulary size — not model size — are the dominant factors limiting success, letting it scale from 33M to 3B-parameter models. Directly applicable to auditing for hidden system-prompt leakage, backdoor detection, and PII exposure.
when_to_use: White-box security auditing where model weights/gradients are available and exact (not just similar) input recovery is required — e.g. formally verifying whether a specific private string could be reconstructed from a model's output.
Backdoor detection: searching for a trigger input that produces an anomalous target output.
when_not_to_use: Only API/black-box query access is available, with no gradient access — use the black-box RPE approach instead.
Long inputs or very large vocabularies, where reconstruction success drops sharply per the paper's own scaling analysis.
known_pitfalls: Reconstruction success degrades substantially as input length and vocabulary size grow — this is an exact-recovery method demonstrated at up to 10 tokens, not a general-purpose long-prompt recovery tool.

primary_source.title: GPT, But Backwards: Search-Based Language Model Inversion

usage_templates.template:
# Setup (requires white-box model access)
Target model: {{target_model}}
Observed output: {{observed_output}}
Initialize a continuous relaxation of a length-{{input_length}} input as one-hot-like vectors over the vocabulary.

# Optimize (repeat up to {{max_steps}} steps)
Compute the objective (how well the current relaxed input, passed through {{target_model}}, reproduces {{observed_output}}) and its gradient with respect to the relaxed input; take an Adam optimizer step.
Every {{reset_interval}} steps, reset the Adam optimizer state to escape local minima in the discrete search space.

# Decode
Once converged, decode the relaxed vectors to the nearest discrete tokens as the reconstructed input.

variables.name: target_model
variables.description: The model being inverted, with white-box (weights/gradients) access

variables.name: observed_output
variables.description: The output whose input is being reconstructed

variables.name: input_length
variables.description: Assumed or known length of the target input in tokens

variables.name: reset_interval
variables.description: How often the optimizer state is periodically reset

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: This template intentionally samples multiple times or explores adaptively; outputs vary run to run by design (explicit temperature>0 sampling, or multi-branch search whose path depends on intermediate stochastic choices).
